Subject: Post-demo follow-up: long-context summarization + truncation behavior

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our call: 

- Problem you described: multi-document legal summaries where single-case contexts frequently exceed 120k tokens; aggressive truncation hurts fidelity for facts across docs.
- Priority: preserve cross-document references (citations, parties) and reduce hallucination when the prompt context is truncated.
- Success metric: extractive recall >= 92% on our 50-sample legal set and summarization F1 improvement vs current baseline.

What we promised to follow up with:
1) Recommended model/profile for long-context evals (fast baseline + high-fidelity option)
2) Benchmark docs and our long-context behavior notes (truncation and KV-cache behavior)
3) Prompt set you shared + an initial mutual action plan for an evaluation run

I attached: redwood-long-context-benchmarks.pdf (notes + sample runs), acme-prompt-set-v2.json (your sample prompts munged to the eval harness), and a starter mutual-action-plan.xlsx.

Recommended next steps:
- We (Redwood) run a 2-day eval on your 50-sample set using the two recommended profiles below.
- Share raw outputs + per-example diffs so your legal SMEs can validate.
- Quick sync next Tuesday to discuss results and pricing for a Dedicated lane if the results look good.

Recommended models/profiles (initial):
- rwf-long-13B-ql (quantized low-latency): good for iterative experimentation; retains ~64k token context with prefix/KV caching.
- rwf-long-70B-hf (high-fidelity): higher quality on cross-document reasoning, supports 128k context in our Dedicated offering; slightly higher cost.

Notes on truncation behavior: our runtime does continuous KV caching + prefix summarization for very long chains. For cases where the total tokens exceed the model window, we can configure a sliding-window summarizer that preserves named entities and legal citations to reduce information loss. Details in the attached PDF.

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm the sample set is representative of the production distribution (cases per doc, avg doc length)?
- Who should own the SME review on your side (Priya or another reviewer)?

Thanks — I’ll queue the eval once you give the go-ahead.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
redwood.ai
